_doc: Electronics tutorials where CircuitQuest's verified circuit (the answer key) is not the only right answer, found by reading the official tutorial by hand. 'differs': the answer key differs from the tutorial and Claude follows the tutorial. 'alternative': the tutorial allows several parts and the answer key picked another. graphgen.evaluate reports accuracy with and without these.

adxl3xx.reason: Official wiring: sensor in A0-A5, code drives A4/A5 as GND/power; the answer key wires it to GND/3.3V.

if-statement.reason: Official tutorial uses the built-in LED; the answer key adds an external LED.

debounce.reason: Answer key's circuit differs from the official tutorial's.

state-change-detection.reason: Answer key's circuit differs from the official tutorial's.

knock.reason: Answer key adds an LED the tutorial does not have.

tone-multiple.reason: Tutorial: speakers with 100 ohm resistors; the answer key differs.

midi.reason: Tutorial: two 220 ohm resistors; the answer key differs.

ping.reason: Same sensor under a different part name in the answer key.

input-pullup-serial.reason: Tutorial uses the internal pull-up; the answer key adds an LED.

pitch-follower.reason: Tutorial: 8 ohm speaker on pin 9 through a 100 ohm resistor, photoresistor with 4.7K; the answer key uses a piezo buzzer with no resistor.

virtual-color-mixer.reason: Tutorial's circuit uses three force-sensing resistors in voltage dividers with 10K resistors; the answer key uses potentiometers.

serial-call-response.reason: Tutorial: '2 analog sensors (potentiometer, photocell, FSR, etc.)' with 10K voltage dividers and '3 10K ohm resistors'; the answer key picked potentiometers with one resistor.

serial-call-response-ascii.reason: Same circuit as serial-call-response: any analog sensor in a 10K voltage divider; the answer key picked potentiometers.

led-bar-graph.reason: Tutorial: 'LED bar graph display or 10 LEDs'; the answer key picked the bar graph.

joystick-mouse-control.reason: Tutorial: one pushbutton on pin 6 (possibly the joystick's own), LED with 220 ohm; the answer key has two buttons on pins 2 and 3 and an LED on pin 5.

calibration.reason: Tutorial: one LED on pin 9 (the built-in LED on 13 shows calibration); the answer key adds an external LED and resistor on pin 13.

while-loop.reason: Tutorial: one LED on pin 9 (the built-in LED on 13 signals calibration); the answer key adds an external LED and resistor on pin 13.

tone-keyboard.reason: Tutorial: an 8 ohm speaker; the answer key uses a piezo buzzer.

arduino-isp.reason: Tutorial shows two set-ups (programming another Arduino board, or an ATmega chip on a breadboard with crystal and capacitors); the answer key picked the chip.

arduino-to-breadboard.reason: Tutorial shows several set-ups (burning the bootloader through an Arduino, or a standalone chip with its blink LED); the answer key picked the standalone chip with the LED.
